title: Replicating Mode Collapse on Open Models: Base vs. RLHF-Aligned Diversity Gap

original_idea.body:
# Replicating Mode Collapse on Open Models: Base vs. RLHF-Aligned Diversity Gap

**Problem:** RLHF-diversity-collapse is mostly demonstrated on proprietary or specific model pairs. A clean base-vs-aligned comparison across several open families would establish how universal the collapse is.

**Direction:** For 3-4 open families with both base and instruct checkpoints, generate many samples per prompt and measure within-model diversity (distinct-n, self-BLEU, Vendi). Twist: test whether aligned models from different families collapse toward each other.

**Why it matters:** Quantifying that alignment both reduces per-model diversity AND pulls models toward a shared distribution operationalizes the systemic-risk mechanism.

**Relevant context:** RLHF-diversity-collapse (arXiv:2310.06452; arXiv:2505.18949) with a cross-family convergence twist tying to Artificial Hivemind.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible: operationalizes the alignment-homogenization mechanism; safety chain indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Base vs instruct checkpoints with standard diversity metrics; no training, accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused base-vs-aligned plus cross-family convergence; well-defined metrics.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open weights, no training; reproducible mechanism evidence labs underpublish.

low_compute.reasoning: Many samples across families; single GPU over time.

novelty.reasoning: RLHF-diversity-collapse already established; mainly replication with a modest convergence twist.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: RLHF diversity collapse well established; cross-family twist is the only novel slice.
